title: Uniform Interior C^{1,alpha} Estimates for Infinity-Harmonic Functions
main_claim: For d>=3 there are alpha_d in (0,1/3] and C_d such that every bounded infinity-harmonic u on B_1 in R^d satisfies ||grad u||_{L^inf(B_1/2)} + [grad u]_{C^{0,alpha_d}(B_1/2)} <= C_d osc_{B_1} u. The proof reduces the estimate, by compactness, to a Liouville theorem for entire solutions of D^2v[(grad_x v,1)]=0 that have sheared affine fits at every center and scale. That theorem is proved using an extremal horizontal Jensen defect, a barycentric-envelope subsolution W, a fair random walk between forward and backward optimizers, localization of contacts near one terminal point, and rigidity from constant envelope slopes.

issues.description: The restriction d>=3 is never used. The Liouville theorem is stated and proved for every m>=1, and the reduction works for any d, so the argument as written would also give the planar case. This is not an error, only an unexplained restriction worth a remark.
issues.evidence: Sec. 3 sets m=d with no dimensional input; Secs. 4-8 hold for general m.

coverage:
I read all of Sections 1-8 in full and re-derived the following by hand:
- Lemma 2.1 (linear lift).
- The cone-slope monotonicity and affine blow-ups.
- Prop 2.5 (three-point flatness): the theorem-of-sums application, the second variation -3Ba^2/(8 sqrt r), and the localization through B_out.
- Lemma 3.2 (uniform flatness), including the scale transfer through the three-point estimate.
- The selection of bad scales (Lambda=32).
- The cylinder-comparison estimates.
- The anisotropic rescaling: the infinity Laplacian equals lambda c^3/r times D^2phi[(grad_x phi,1+lambda phi_t)].
- The normalized fit domain, C_0=256, and the argument that an affine limit gives a contradiction.
- The Hölder exponent gamma/(2+gamma).
- The frame-change covariance and the fit-parameter log bounds (a-a'+|p-p'|^2/2 identity).
- The path-convexity of P_ell (Hessian |d|^2/ell along (q,1)).
- The envelope-slope order.
- The barycentric duality.
- The common-time sum rule, and the barycentric-subsolution corollary: the variance term (t0+h)/(2t0^2) sum theta|y_i-x0|^2 is affine along the motion.
- The nonaffine-slice argument and the attainment of the extremal kappa through tight measures.
- The finiteness of H_v(z_*) through the chord inequality and the Jensen-equality transfer.
- Lemma 6.1, including the quadratic identity -(t/(2 ell s))|y-(s/t)x|^2.
- The exact drift identity and the constant 1/(16(1+log2)).
- The fitted-frame invariance of the velocity discrepancies.
- The log velocity bound.
- The walk estimates: visit counts, Doob/Cauchy-Schwarz travel, cutoff probabilities 3/4-1/8-1/8.
- The weak-limit and Portmanteau steps for contact at the marks, H_v(z_end)>-inf, and limsup localization.
- The final rigidity lemma (q_+=q_- and the squeeze V=A).
- The preservation of the barycentric gap kappa^2/2 in the final limit.
I did not run any numerical checks; the algebra was checked by hand.
